text:
maria: Quick sync — I'm putting together a small schema pipeline so runtime/infra can publish a minimal, stable set of metrics that the Console dashboards and rollouts UX can depend on. Want to lock label names + cardinality guardrails today. Draft doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/metrics-schema (editable).

sameer: +1. main concern is high-cardinality labels leaking into dashboards (request_id, prompt_hash, client_uuid). We need clear must/optional/prohibit lists.

olivia: Agreed. Minimal labels I think: service, model, route, region, env, tier. Optional: deployment, quantization (q4_q8 etc). Prohibit: request_id, user_message_id, full_prompt.

kevin: Do we need model_version vs model_name? Console needs both for rollouts. Suggest: model (name), model_version (semver or git sha), model_variant (quantized|fp16).

maria: Yes Kevin — include model_version. Also we need a small set of routing labels for per-route SLOs: route, route_owner, priority. Keep route_owner low-cardinality (team name).

elaine: From infra side — make sure OTel exporter maps these labels consistently. We should define the canonical Prom label names now: service, model, model_version, model_variant, route, route_owner, region, env, tier, deployment. Any more?

sameer: Add backend (runtime|cache|fallback) — useful for rollouts to see fallback counts.

olivia: +backend. On cardinality: recommend max 50 unique values for route_owner, 200 for model_version in active time window, region/env/tier should be tiny. If we see exploding cardinality, auto-strip to `other`.

maria: Good. Can we standardize naming conventions: prom metric names should be prefix `redwood_runtime_` and snake_case. Example: `redwood_runtime_inference_latency_seconds_bucket`. Labels in curly braces.

kevin: Example snippet for ops team and docs:```promql
# Histogram for inference latency per model+route
redwood_runtime_inference_latency_seconds_bucket{service="runtime", model="gpt-4o", model_version="2026-02-12", route="/v1/generate", region="us-west1", env="prod", backend="runtime"}
```

elaine: Nice. Also add an internal label `ingestion_node` that infra uses for debug, but ensure it's dropped from Console by default. We can mark it telemetry.only=true in schema.

maria: Plan proposal: 1) finalize canonical labels this week, 2) runtime/infra add exporter mapping + test data, 3) eng-platform wires labels into dashboard templates (with cardinality guards), 4) rollout in canary, monitor cardinality for 2 weeks.

sameer: Sounds right. One ask: add a lightweight linter in CI that warns on metrics with prohibited labels. I'll open a PR.

olivia: I can add a migration note for teams that have custom metrics. We'll provide a mapping table and fallback rules (`label_rewrite_map`).

kevin: Also surface a small histogram+counter set that Console assumes for rollouts: `inference_latency` (histogram), `inference_requests_total` (counter), `inference_errors_total` (counter), `inference_fallbacks_total` (counter). All with the canonical labels.

maria: Exactly. I'll add those to the doc and create dashboard JSON templates.

deploy-bot: deploy: metrics-schema-draft v0.1 -> staging at 2026-03-07T15:12:30Z :white_check_mark:

elaine: After deploy, infra will run a 24h smoke to verify label cardinality and tag volumes. We'll post results in this thread.

maria: Thanks everyone. If no objections, I'll freeze label names at EOD and ping for PRs. :thumbsup:
